title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows + optimize cache and parallelism (hygiene)
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Our monolithic CI workflows have become slow and brittle as more repositories and build matrices were added. This PR splits the heavyweight combined workflow into focused jobs (lint, unit-test, integration-test, release) and improves cache hygiene and parallelism to reduce queue times and false cache misses. Changes: 1) Split workflows: - .github/workflows/lint.yml: extracted linters (eslint, golangci-lint, markdownlint) with a small matrix per language to minimize warmup. - .github/workflows/test.yml: unit and integration tests separated; unit tests run with a fast Node matrix and JS dependency cache restores; integration tests run on-demand via workflow_dispatch for expensive infra. - .github/workflows/release.yml: release automation isolated, with guard rails and a `release-dry-run` job. 2) Cache hygiene and restoration: standardize cache keys (OS-arch-language-restore-keys) and add step ordering to ensure package manager lockfiles are used as the primary key. 3) Parallelism and job sizing: reduce batch sizes for long-running tests and increase job concurrency for lint jobs to reduce overall CI wall time while keeping resource usage under org quota. 4) Actions and deps: bump actions/checkout to v4, setup-node to v4, and consolidate frequently used composite actions into .github/actions/common to reduce duplication. 5) Observability: add workflow-level-duration metric emit (via echoing to workflow output for the metrics collector) and CI tag in test reporters. Checklist: - [x] Split workflows and validate local/remote runs - [x] Confirm cache hit/miss improvements on staging CI - [x] Run full test matrix on branch (stability run) - [x] Get approvals from infra and platform - [x] Update docs/ci.md with new workflow boundaries Backwards compatibility: no runtime code changes; developer git hooks and local scripts untouched. Risks & mitigations: cache-key changes could cause initial cold caches (mitigated by progressive rollout and keeping old keys for one week), release workflow split could change timing for release-notes generation (mitigated by dry-run and feature flag). Related: ENG-9482 (CI stability) and SUP-1123 (support escalations for flaky release jobs).
